limits.step_unit: none: x1sim reports no step count (systems/algol-60/README.md, Units; harnesses/QUESTIONS.md Q12)

confounds: The harness writes on the program's standard input: one line of instance parameters, then one message line per stage, replayed stage, replayed commitment or spawned computation, each message that poses or replays stage k followed by stage k's lines of the constants file with their 'k:' tag removed (README, 2.2). No stage's constants are on the input before the stage is posed. This is how a stage is passed in; it is listed because the program reads it with the configuration's input procedures, whose calls are H.

Answers, observe() state, emit entries and the end of a stage are taken from the program's printed tags ([answer]...[/answer], [observe]...[/observe], [emit]...[/emit], [end]) by pattern matching on the standard output; the text between tags is kept verbatim. Answers beyond a query's cap are left in stdout and print but not collected.

A spawned computation (P09) is a procedure of the one program, started by the harness's spawn message, and runs to its end, budget or error before the next is spawned (side_by_side false). ALGOL 60 has no mechanism for separate computations; see QUESTIONS.md.

x1sim compiles the program to an object file beside it, so the harness copies the program into a fresh temporary directory as prog.a60 and runs x1sim there, with HOME set to that directory and X1ALGOL_LIB unset, so that the library is /usr/local/lib/x1algol.lib.
x1sim has no step count, so no budget is enforced; only the safety limit stops it (QUESTIONS.md Q12 of the common part).

execution_state.basis: the program wrote [end] and asked for its next message; ALGOL 60 holds no alternatives or suspended work of its own, so the state is read from the program's [alternatives] and [suspended] reports in its observe block (alternatives 0, suspended 0)
